original_text:
All the DSA resources I used to crack Google (2025) -

📺 𝗬𝗼𝘂𝗧𝘂𝗯𝗲 𝗖𝗵𝗮𝗻𝗻𝗲𝗹𝘀

1. Striver A2Z DSA Playlist
https://lnkd.in/gJXB9cnY
Covers everything from basics to advanced DSA with pseudocode clarity. Builds real problem-solving intuition.

2. Vivek Gupta’s Dynamic Programming Workshop
https://lnkd.in/g62GukQS
Laser-focused on advanced DP patterns and transitions. Great for mastering optimization-heavy problems.

3. Aditya Verma’s DP Playlist
https://lnkd.in/gaF9JE92
Breaks down how recursion evolves into DP. Best suited for those starting their DP journey.

📚 𝗪𝗲𝗯𝘀𝗶𝘁𝗲𝘀 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗮𝗯𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝗮𝗹𝗴𝗼𝗿𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗺𝘀

1. CP-Algorithms
https://cp-algorithms.com
Encyclopedia of high-level algorithms - from suffix arrays to heavy-light decomposition. Perfect for deep dives.

2. USACO Guide
https://usaco.guide
A curated roadmap with problem sets, concepts, and video explanations. Helps you rise from beginner to elite.


🏆 𝗣𝗿𝗮𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗰𝗲 𝗣𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺𝘀

1. LeetCode
https://leetcode.com
Most popular interview platform. Weekly contests emulate the exact pace and pressure of real FAANG rounds.

2. AtCoder Educational DP Contest
https://lnkd.in/g4WYiA4p
26 hand-crafted problems to learn DP the right way - with clean, editorial-backed insights.

3. CSES Problem Set
https://cses.fi/problemset
Graph algorithms. Trees. 100+ well-thought-out problems to master core concepts.

4. Codeforces
https://codeforces.com
Legendary contests that challenge your mathematical and logical reasoning under tight time pressure.

There’s no secret formula. Just the right resources, ruthless consistency, and clear fundamentals.

Save this. 
…see more

ai_analysis.summary: This is a resource list for Google and FAANG-style algorithm interview preparation rather than a Data Engineering post. It recommends YouTube resources for learning data structures and algorithms and dynamic programming, two curated learning references, and four platforms for practice. The recommendations range from DSA fundamentals and beginner DP to advanced patterns, high-level algorithms, graph and tree problems, and timed contests. The post emphasizes consistency and clear fundamentals but provides no study schedule or secret formula. The supplied content appears truncated after “Save this,” and no additional media text was provided.
subtopics: DSA fundamentals through advanced problem solving
Progression from recursion to dynamic programming
Mathematical and logical reasoning under time pressure

interview_questions.question: Which listed resources are intended for learners beginning dynamic programming, and how do their approaches differ?
interview_questions.answer:
Aditya Verma’s DP Playlist is intended for learners starting DP and explains how recursion evolves into DP.
The AtCoder Educational DP Contest provides 26 editor-backed problems for practicing DP.
Vivek Gupta’s workshop is positioned as a more advanced resource focused on DP patterns and transitions.

interview_questions.question: Which resources does the post recommend for progressing from DSA fundamentals to advanced algorithm study?
interview_questions.answer:
The Striver A2Z DSA Playlist covers basics through advanced DSA and emphasizes pseudocode clarity.
CP-Algorithms supports deep study of high-level algorithms, including suffix arrays and heavy-light decomposition.
The USACO Guide provides a structured roadmap with concepts, problem sets, and video explanations.

interview_questions.question: How can the listed practice platforms support preparation for timed algorithm interviews?
interview_questions.answer:
LeetCode weekly contests emulate the pace and pressure of real FAANG rounds.
Codeforces contests develop mathematical and logical reasoning under tight time limits.
CSES supplies more than 100 graph and tree problems for mastering core concepts.
AtCoder provides a focused set of DP problems supported by editorial-backed insights.
